input.quote: 10.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
input.rationale: Section 10.5 selects New York law, which is our preferred governing law, and there is no arbitration clause anywhere in the Agreement (searches for arbitration, venue, courts and dispute resolution returned nothing). However, the Agreement contains no forum or jurisdiction provision at all, so the second element of the preferred position (and the forum element of the fallback) is unmet, leaving venue open to any court either party chooses. We therefore add a single sentence conferring exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County, with a carve-out only for temporary injunctive relief, and leave the existing governing-law wording untouched.

ops.text: The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York shall have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits of any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement, provided that either Party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction.
